linguistic_propositions.proposition: A pair counts as complete paronomasia only when the two tokens agree in letter inventory, letter count, letter order and vocalisation, and diverge solely in sense.
Incomplete paronomasia is defined negatively as any single divergence in letter identity, letter count, letter order or vowel quality while audible resemblance is retained.
Semantic divergence is criterial: two occurrences of one token in one and the same sense are plain repetition, not paronomasia.
Antithesis requires only opposition of sense between two elements co-occurring in the same clause or span; no sound relation is imposed.
A term paired with its own negated counterpart is a full instance of antithesis rather than a defective one.
Incomplete paronomasia occurs more often than complete paronomasia in Arabic because exact homophony is rare.
Any homophony accompanied by semantic divergence qualifies as paronomasia irrespective of register or authorial intent.
One token bearing two senses across a discourse counts as paronomasia.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Rhymed prose is constituted by two or more successive clauses sharing a final rhyme; unlike verse it imposes no fixed metrical template.
The divergent subtype requires only the shared rhyme letter and tolerates different morphological templates on the rhyming words.
The studded subtype additionally requires the internal words of the paired clauses to correspond in morphological template, not only the final words.
The balanced subtype requires approximate equality of clause length together with template agreement on the final words, while leaving internal words unconstrained.
Parallelism requires at least two pairs; a single opposed pair is classified as contrariety instead.
Subtype assignment for rhymed prose is decidable from clause-internal structure rather than from the endings alone.
Clause length is measured in approximate syllable count for the balanced subtype.
Scripture uses rhymed prose extensively and literary rhymed prose derives resonance from that association.
Correspondence is a near-synonym of parallelism in some usages.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: In the double-entendre figure a single polysemous token carries a readier sense and a remoter sense, and only the remoter one is intended.
The readier sense is not an error; it is a licit reading deliberately left unintended, so both senses must be independently available for the word.
The remoter sense is called remote because it costs the hearer an inferential step, not because it is unrelated to the word.
The double-entendre figure involves one token with two senses, whereas the sound-based figure involves two distinct tokens that resemble each other.
Invented causation attributes a fictional reason for an event, as distinct from metaphor which predicates one thing of another.
Word compatibility is a passage-level property arising jointly from phonetic resemblance, shared semantic field, shared emotional register and shared morphological template.
Identifying invented causation presupposes knowing the real cause of the described event.
Where a text explicitly announces both senses of a token, the double-entendre figure is still in force.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A meter is individuated by which feet it uses, how many times they repeat per hemistich, and which variations it licenses.
The long meter's hemistich is the alternation of a three-syllable foot with a longer foot, twice, totalling twenty-four morae.
A deviation from the nominal foot in a licensed position is a permitted licence rather than a metrical error.
The final syllable of a hemistich is conventionally scanned as heavy irrespective of its actual weight.
Feet decompose into a two-syllable sabab and a three-syllable watid.
The core-foot table's stated syllable counts and weight strings are internally consistent with the light/heavy definitions used elsewhere in the module.
The worked scansion string for the sample hemistich matches the syllable list from which it was derived.
The tradition credits the founder with fifteen meters and a student with a sixteenth.
Close to a third of classical Arabic verse is composed in the long meter.
Metrical regularity is usable as an authenticity test for transmitted verse.
Metrical patterning also underlies prose rhythm and recitation, not only verse.

'one deviation disproves the meter' — ignores the licence system

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A light syllable is a consonant plus a short vowel; a heavy syllable is a consonant plus a long vowel, or a consonant plus a short vowel plus a closing consonant.
Arabic metre measures duration rather than stress, each light syllable counting one mora and each heavy syllable two.
A voweled consonant followed by another voweled consonant yields a light syllable; a voweled consonant followed by a quiescent consonant or by a long vowel yields a heavy syllable.
Indefinite endings are realised in scansion as a closing nasal consonant, converting the final syllable to heavy.
The article assimilates to a following coronal letter and is written in the assimilated form for scansion.
Certain demonstrative and particle spellings conceal a long vowel that scansion must restore.
A hemistich-final short vowel may be lengthened for the rhyme and scanned as heavy.
Syllable weight classification under the light/heavy labels is the contribution of the early grammarian named in the narrative passage.
The rewrite table's row on the feminine ending is stated correctly and its worked example instantiates that rule.
The summary rule block distinguishes the three indefinite endings in its transcriptions.
Ordinary short utterances in unpolished speech already realise metrical patterns, so meters were discovered rather than invented.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Inflectional vowels are realised only in continuous delivery and are neutralised to zero at a pause, so a pausal utterance carries no audible case or mood.
Two of the three indefinite endings are neutralised at a pause while the accusative one surfaces as a long vowel, because its supporting letter is written.
The feminine ending is realised as a voiceless glottal-final consonant at a pause rather than as a stop.
Pause sites are classified as complete, sufficient, good or corrupting, according to whether the meaning is finished and whether what follows depends on what precedes.
A pause that leaves a governed element separated from its governor corrupts the reading and is prohibited.
Pause placement can change which element is construed as subject and how far a negation extends.
A supporting consonant is added at a pause after certain endings, including after long vowels generally.
The marker set listed for the mushaf is the standard inventory and its five symbols carry the stated instructions.
Vocalisation dotting was introduced by a named early figure and the vocalisation signs in current use were devised by the founder of prosody, who also established the pausing rules.
Pausing after a bare negator yields the opposite of the intended assertion.
Pausing and connecting belong to grammar and not only to recitation technique.
